interest: This document is particularly interesting to historians because it illustrates how the United States government monitored Japanese commercial fishing operations as potential national security and espionage threats across the Pacific Basin immediately prior to and during World War II. It highlights inter-agency intelligence coordination among the State Department, War Department, Department of the Interior, Office of Censorship, and Congress—such as Senator Millard Tydings' alert regarding fraudulent crew substitutions on Japanese merchant and fishing vessels. Furthermore, the docket entries trace the complex intersection of resource competition, wartime domestic food shortages in Japan, Mexican maritime enforcement, and Soviet-Japanese diplomatic relations surrounding salmon concessions in Kamchatka.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet (SAN Sheet #36) for decimal classification 894.628 (Fisheries - Japan), recording documents catalogued between December 1940 and October 1942. The indexed entries track diplomatic despatches, voluntary consular reports, congressional correspondence, military notifications, and intelligence intercepts concerning Japanese fishing activities and marine industries across the Pacific and adjacent waters. Key subjects include Japanese fishing fleets in the Bering Sea, U.S. policy regarding Japanese participation in Alaskan salmon fisheries, concerns raised by Senator Millard E. Tydings over clandestine Japanese crew rotations, the all-Japanese manning of the vessel Amano following the departure of a Danish crewman, Mexican arrests of Japanese fishing boats including the Yoshino and Ryono, wartime fish shortages in Japan, salmon fishing concessions in Kamchatka, and an Office of Censorship intercept concerning the Japan-Russian Fishing Company. Most underlying records were routed or cross-referenced to other decimal files, including 894.85, 894.20212, and 811.628.

subfiles.about: A State Department docket control sheet cataloguing incoming and outgoing documents concerning Japanese fisheries and maritime security between December 1940 and October 1942.
subfiles.summary: This list of papers (SAN Sheet #36) summarizes eleven documents (sub-numbers 216 through 225) filed under decimal number 894.628 between December 1940 and October 1942. The entries record diplomatic reports, congressional inquiries, inter-departmental memoranda, and intelligence intercepts concerning Japanese commercial fishing operations, potential espionage, crew substitutions, and vessel seizures across the Pacific, Bering Sea, Alaska, the U.S. West Coast, Mexico, and Kamchatka. The sheet also documents cross-references and transfers of primary records to other State Department decimal files, including 894.85, 894.20212, and 811.628.
